evaluator: Final holdout A — PR-015, Prof. Margaret Morse lens
evidence: The About page directly connects the practice as “artistic, civic, technical, and social,” with links to WOWList, Sunday Dinner/196, FairRentNYC, and Source-Backed Team Memory—all reachable within one additional click.

At least three distinct continuities are explicit: WOWList turns community vocabulary into participatory publishing infrastructure; Sunday Dinner/196 turns hospitality and trust into repeatable hosting and onboarding; FairRentNYC turns meetings, public sources, and civic participation into campaign memory and action pathways; HJE turns customer knowledge and institutional voice into maintained technical operations.
The recurring method is plainly stated: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue.

Project-specific differences remain legible: commercial stewardship at HJE, decentralized cultural discovery in WOWList, resident-facing data translation in CallNYC, consent-bound hospitality at Sunday Dinner/196, coalition documentation in FairRentNYC, and human-reviewed knowledge practice in the lab.

Reciprocal agency is visible through participant governance, community language shaping WOWList, collaborators using and continuing coalition records, people shaping the Sunday Dinner/196 practice, and repeated co-built, collective, and collaborator-led framing.

Job fit remains prominent through the homepage’s role-oriented paths, the Technical Operations & Implementation proof map, explicit capability language, transferable-proof sections, and hiring-team summaries.

Collective credit is consistently bounded: WOWList is co-built; FairRentNYC explicitly rejects sole causation; campaign outcomes remain collective; HJE credits the company team; Sunday Dinner/196 credits its community.

Privacy boundaries are explicit across the reviewed surfaces, excluding private dashboards, customer data, coalition notes, legal-review materials, correspondence, guest histories, contact details, access information, and unapproved images or quotations.

The public course-completion certificate is correctly bounded as professional development, not instructor affiliation, endorsement, production-SaaS evidence, or proof that the lab is a finished product.
safety_findings: No visible use of private UCSC narrative evaluations, private correspondence, or unapproved testimonials was found in the reviewed copy and links.
The lab’s public course-completion artifact stays within the permitted boundary and includes an explicit limiting caption.
Archived CallNYC content is clearly labeled unofficial, historical, and unsuitable as current constituent-service guidance.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 unchanged. The visible portfolio establishes an interdisciplinary operating lineage while preserving project difference, reciprocal agency, role clarity, collective credit, privacy, and protected-source boundaries.
